posts.author: JohnDoeGames
posts.body:
So, you might know my plugin, the clock and calendar one. It was based on a free workshop, but now it is a payed plugin.
And that payed part, that is something not everyone likes... So some people try to find a free copy uploaded by pirates. They google things like "johndoenews bootleg" or "johndoenews free download". Someone even tried: "Wanna trade payed plugins? I am looking for johndoenews calendar"
But then, when they can't find it (since it is brand new...), they click on the first link in the search engine, which is my website... And I can see which key words are used to find my website.
Here is the funny part: Each time that happened (3 times this week),
it happened less than a minute after someone was linked from RPGmakerweb to my itch page
.
Conclusion... Someone on RPGmakerweb really, really wants to use my plugins, but they don't feel like paying.
Beware of thieves, people!!!
We may work hard to try and make an honest buck (some of us even do that on top of a fulltime job...) but others want everything for free and have no intention to work for anything.
I know my plugin is amazing, but it is not that amazing and that expensive that people turn into criminals to get it.

Most websites can see that. My website is build on Blogger, which is a google service. That makes seeing key words in google a lot easier, but on itch.io and such, you can also see which link people followed to come to your project.
Pirates are really not that smart... They know how to bend the rules to get what they want, but they forget that we are skilled with computers too. I already found that 3 attempts are made by 2 different people. (1 person tried twice). I know the countries they are from, and I know the gmail adres of the one who tried to pirate me twice. This will lead to me knowing their usernames on Itch and on RPG maker web. And once I have those, I can take real action*.
(*Edit: Real action would be reporting them to have them banned on those platforms. I'm not a hacker.)
They tried to rip of the wrong guy.
Note that all info I found was public. I didn't have to break any laws to get the info I got. And before the match is over, I will know so much more.

If you click a link on a google website, google registers which link is clicked, that link is different, if you use different key words. So... No matter what you do in your computer and how much your close up your browser, the number of visits on that link, are the number of clicks connected to those key words.
That happens all on the google website.
If you really want to do it without being part of the statistics, you need to copy the link instead of clicking it, then paste it in the address bar, and than remove everything that isn't part of the URL location... But that only works if you know which part of the link is location and which part is data.
If we take youtube for example... When you look at the adress bar when watching a video, it will have a rather long URL... Even though when you click on share, you get a very short URL, but still longer than the actual link.
The rest is traffic data, telling google how you got to that video.
look.... This is a share-window of youtube...
That is a link to my video, but the actual link it:
Code:
https://youtu.be/oufNg6T-aL0
The ? and everything that comes after, that is google tracking what site links to where.
